# Re-entrant lifecycles latch on a generation, never on a flag

<!-- review-bot-scope:start -->
packages/store-libsql/src/**/*.ts
packages/core/src/**/*.ts
packages/sdk/src/**/*.ts
packages/driver/src/**/*.ts
packages/conformance/src/**/*.ts
specs/*.tla
<!-- review-bot-scope:end -->

Scope: `packages/store-libsql/src/**/*.ts`, `packages/core/src/**/*.ts`, `packages/sdk/src/**/*.ts`, `packages/driver/src/**/*.ts`, `packages/conformance/src/**/*.ts`, `specs/*.tla`. This rule asks exactly one question of any state that records "this already happened": can the thing it describes legitimately happen AGAIN, and does the latch carry WHICH occurrence it happened for? Deliberately NOT covered here: whether a follow-on keys on its batch's own stamp and the post-transition state (DESIGN §3.4 rules 1 and 8) — that belongs to the batch-provenance/fenced-follow-on rule; terminal-state inertness (rule 6), where being one-way IS the invariant; clock sources (rule 3). A guard can be flawlessly fenced and still be a one-shot flag; this rule reads only that second half.

**The invariant.** A run row is re-claimed many times in one life — every sleep wake, every lost-launch relaunch, every chain hop — so, in DESIGN §3.2's words, "a one-shot flag can never work". The latch that phrase rejects is "the run has started": `started_at IS NULL`. Trace it through today's code. The first sleep wake re-claims the row; the second claim's launch is delivered; activation refuses it because the run started once already; the worker exits; `sweep` classifies by `activated_gen < claim_gen` (`store.ts:647`), reads a launch that never arrived, and reopens the run. With `RELAUNCH_CAP = 5` and 5–60s linear backoff (`core/src/contract.ts`), five reopens later `sweepLostLaunch`'s `cap` arm fails the run AND its task terminally with `$RelaunchCapExhausted` (`store.ts:682-720`). Every workflow that slept even once would die about a minute later reporting a launcher failure that never happened — nothing thrown, nothing logged, the failure reason naming the wrong subsystem. This one was caught at design time and never shipped; the rule exists because the shape is cheap to reintroduce and its symptom always accuses a healthy subsystem.

The answer is not a bigger cap or a reset somewhere: activation is a per-claim compare-and-set — `WHERE run_id = ? AND queue = ? AND claimed_by = ? AND state = 'running' AND claim_gen = ? AND activated_gen < ?` (`store.ts:485-486`) — with the claim bumping `claim_gen` and the launch payload carrying it. CLAUDE.md carries the generalization as the first entry on the prevention ladder's precedent list: *"the one-shot activation flag → no one-shot flags for re-entrant lifecycles, latch on generations."* Any state that can legitimately be entered more than once latches on a monotonic ordinal or a per-occurrence token, never on a boolean, a nullness test, or a once-set timestamp.

<!-- review-bot-synopsis:start -->
Flag a transition admitted by a flag it also sets (`SET started_at_ms = now … WHERE started_at_ms IS NULL`, `WHERE activated_gen = 0`, a new `0/1`/`…_done`/`active` column or nullable timestamp on runs/tasks/waits read as `IS NULL`/`= 0` to permit a re-enterable transition); an ordinal (`claim_gen`, `activated_gen`, `attempt`, `owner_attempt`, `relaunch_count`, `infra_retries`) guarded with `<>`/`!=` or against a literal instead of the monotone `activated_gen < :claim_gen`; an ordinal reset to `0`/`NULL` or written from a `COUNT(*)` over deletable rows; a new re-entry path whose transition keeps a quoted flag guard; an in-process per-occurrence value matched on a repeating key (event name not step key, `runId` not `(runId, claimGen)`) or never consumed, or a never-reset field/"seen" set on an object outliving the occurrence; a TLA action for a re-entrant transition guarded on a boolean rather than an ordinal; and a new generation CAS shipped with no conformance case where a SECOND occurrence PASSES it plus an invariant bounding the ordinal. Pass for nullable timestamps read as DUE times paired with a clock comparison (`available_at_ms IS NOT NULL AND <= now`, `cancelDue`), once-ever FACTS that gate nothing (`started_at_ms`/`first_started_at_ms` COALESCE beside `activated_gen < :claim_gen`), CAS guards on the re-enterable pre-state (`state = 'running'`, `relaunch_count < RELAUNCH_CAP`), column-to-column ordinal comparisons that classify sweep arms (`activated_gen = claim_gen`, `activated_gen < claim_gen`), existence tests on a per-occurrence token or minted identity (claim's `NOT EXISTS … claimed_by = ?`, spawn's two `NOT EXISTS`, `successorOwned` keyed by task and intended attempt), once-per-KEY lifecycles (`emitEvent` first-write-wins, `awaitEvent`'s `NOT EXISTS events`, the `applied:vN` sentinel with its previous-value-guarded bump), latches scoped to one occurrence and rebuilt per claim (`pendingWake`/`takeWake`, finally-reset `inStep`, `seen`/`nameUses`, per-pass AbortControllers, `FencedBatch`'s local `won`), single-use objects that throw (`DriverLoop.everRan`), conformance checkers and hand-seeded fixture rows, TLA one-shots the model documents (`firstStarted`, `eventState`), and the PR3.8 wait-identity deferral BUILD.md already owns.
<!-- review-bot-synopsis:end -->

Report a failure when the changed code introduces any of these:

- **A transition admitted by a flag it also sets.** The WHERE says a column is unset and the SET writes it: `SET started_at_ms = ${NOW} … WHERE … started_at_ms IS NULL`, `WHERE activated_gen = 0`, `WHERE handled = 0 … SET handled = 1`. Includes a new `0/1` INTEGER, a `..._done`/`is_…`/`active`/`handled` column, or a nullable timestamp added to `runs`, `tasks` or `waits` in the same diff to serve as that guard. `runs` rows are re-claimed, re-activated, reopened and re-parked; a `waits` row can be re-registered at the same `(run_id, step_name)` when a run replays through the same await. The correct shape compares a stored ordinal against the caller's carried value (`activated_gen < :claim_gen`) or matches a per-occurrence token (`claimed_by = :token AND claim_gen = :claim_gen`).
- **An ordinal guarded with `<>`/`!=`, or against a literal.** `activated_gen <> :claim_gen` re-admits an OLDER generation, so a stale launch delivered after a re-claim activates; `activated_gen = 0` grants exactly one activation for the row's entire life — the case `suite.ts:1054` pins ("an `'= 0'` classifier would misfire here"). Applies to `claim_gen`, `activated_gen`, `attempt`, `owner_attempt`, `relaunch_count`, `infra_retries`, and any ordinal the diff introduces. `= :param` binding the caller's carried generation is the correct shape, not this one.
- **An ordinal reset, or written from a count.** `SET claim_gen = 0`, `relaunch_count = NULL`, or an ordinal SET from a `COUNT(*)` over rows that get deleted (`waits` are reaped at claim, complete, fail, both sweeps and cancel), which makes it go backwards. The lost-launch reopen deliberately leaves `claim_gen` untouched (`store.ts:669-675`) so a stale in-flight launch dies on the gen guard after the next claim.
- **A new re-entry path whose transition keeps a flag guard.** The diff adds another way to reach an existing transition (a relaunch, a re-delivery, a resume, a chain hop, a second caller) and the guard admitting that transition is one of the shapes above. The bug is in the untouched guard, not the new caller — so QUOTE the guard; if you cannot quote it, there is no finding.
- **In-process: a per-occurrence value matched on a key that repeats.** A carried wake, delivery, memo or "already handled" record matched by something not unique to the occurrence — the event NAME rather than the await's step key, `runId` rather than `(runId, claimGen)` — or a carried value with no consume path, so a second occurrence re-reads the first's. This is what `ReplayContext.pendingWake`/`takeWake(stepKey)` (`sdk/src/context.ts:86-114`) exists to make structural; matching wakes by event name was the worst defect of the events round (`postmortems/pr11-events-review.md`, finding 1: durable false timeouts on a retry loop). Also here: a field flipped true with no path back, or a `Set`/`Map` "seen" set not keyed by the occurrence, on an object that outlives one occurrence (`DriverLoop`, the worker pump, a launcher).
- **A TLA action for a re-entrant transition guarded on a boolean.** `~activated[r]` / `activated' = [activated EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]`, where `Scheduler.tla` models the ordinal (`claimGen`, `activatedGen`, guard `activatedGen[m.run] < m.gen` at line 612). Spec-first means the shape ships to SQL, and the model would then prove the wrong protocol correct.
- **A new per-occurrence latch with no executable twin.** The diff adds or moves a generation CAS and adds no conformance case in which a SECOND occurrence PASSES the latch after the first — the shape of `suite.ts:128-155`, *"rejects stale tokens and stale generations after a re-claim"*, which asserts both halves — and no invariant arm bounding the new ordinal, the way `generation-or-counter-corrupt` (`conformance/src/invariants.ts:271-275`) makes `activated_gen > claim_gen` impossible. A test that only shows a duplicate delivery being refused stays green under a one-shot flag.

Allowed cases (do NOT flag these):

- **A nullable timestamp read as a DUE time, not as "already happened".** `claim`'s `r.available_at_ms IS NOT NULL AND r.available_at_ms <= ${NOW}` (`store.ts:365,372`), `SWEEP_SCAN_EXPIRED_SQL`'s `claim_expires_at_ms IS NOT NULL AND … <= ${NOW_MS}` (`store.ts:167`), the `waits-timeout` narrow (`store.ts:437-438`), `NEXT_WAKE_SQL`, and `cancelDue`/`cancelNotDue` (`fragments.ts:102-107`). The nullness means "no deadline armed" and is always paired with a comparison to an instant, so the same row is admitted again the next time it comes due.
- **A once-ever FACT that gates nothing.** `activate` writes `started_at_ms = COALESCE(started_at_ms, ${NOW})` (`store.ts:481`) and its `task-start` follow-on writes `first_started_at_ms = COALESCE(first_started_at_ms, …)` (`store.ts:515`). These look exactly like the forbidden shape and are correct: the admission decision is `activated_gen < :claim_gen` on the line above, and the COALESCE only stops a later legitimate activation from overwriting a value that means "the first time". A latch on a *value* is fine; a latch on *permission* is not.
- **A CAS guarded on the re-enterable pre-state it consumes.** `state = 'running'`, `state IN ('pending','running','sleeping')`, `relaunch_count < RELAUNCH_CAP`, `claim_expires_at_ms <= ${NOW}`. Re-satisfiable on the next occurrence, and they are what makes a replay of the batch match nothing.
- **Column-to-column ordinal comparisons that CLASSIFY.** `sweep`'s `item.activatedGen < item.claimGen` (`store.ts:647`), `sweepLostLaunch`'s `activated_gen < claim_gen` (`store.ts:660-661`) and `sweepClaimTimeout`'s `AND activated_gen = claim_gen` (`store.ts:753`) pick which arm applies to a run that has already been claimed; neither is a one-shot latch.
- **An existence test whose subject is the per-occurrence token or a freshly minted identity.** `claim`'s receipt guard `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM runs held WHERE held.queue = ? AND held.state = 'running' AND held.claimed_by = ?)` (`store.ts:382-385`, §3.4 rule 4); `spawn`'s `WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tasks x WHERE x.task_id = ?)` (`store.ts:248`) and `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM runs r WHERE r.task_id = f.task_id)` (`store.ts:289`, whose comment is the argument: "Asking whether the task already has a run is a question about ownership, which does not decay"); `successorOwned(id, task, intendedAttempt)` (`fragments.ts`), an EXISTS probe over every immutable field of the freshly minted successor.
- **Once-per-KEY lifecycles where the occurrence lives in the key.** `emitEvent`'s payload is first-write-wins on `(queue, event_name)`, while its conflict update is guarded by `events.fence_stamp IS NOT ${STAMP}`: a fresh delivery token may establish a new execution fence, but `fence_at_ms` is always the immutable `emitted_at_ms`, so exact replay stays on that instant even after another token overwrites the receipt. `awaitEvent`'s `WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM events WHERE queue = ? AND event_name = ?)` sees that immutable event fact (DESIGN §3.8.3; `Scheduler.tla:137-138`). Likewise the migration runner's `INSERT INTO meta … ('applied:v<N>', '1')` sentinel plus `UPDATE meta SET value = ? WHERE key = 'schema_version' AND value = ?` (`admin.ts:108,113`) — a version number IS the generation and the bump is a monotone CAS on the previous value.
- **A latch whose scope is exactly one occurrence.** `ReplayContext.pendingWake`/`takeWake`, the finally-reset `inStep`, and the `seen`/`nameUses` maps (`sdk/src/context.ts:76-78,161-167`) — a new claim builds a new `ReplayContext`, so all of them are rebuilt per generation and keyed per await; the per-pass `pumpStop`/`leaseLost` AbortControllers (`sdk/src/run-worker.ts:112-113`) and `withLaunchTimeout`'s `settled` (`driver/src/loop.ts:294`); `FencedBatch.run`'s local `won` (`core/src/fenced-batch.ts:466`); `fault-matrix.ts:320`'s local `let done`.
- **A genuinely single-use object that fails loudly.** `DriverLoop.everRan` (`driver/src/loop.ts:75,157-163`) is a plain boolean that throws `DriverLoop.run() is one-shot — construct a new loop to restart`. The lifecycle really is once per instance, restart means a new instance, and the refusal is an exception rather than a silent no-op — the property that separates it from the activation shape.
- **Checkers and fixtures in the conformance package.** `invariants.ts` asserts corruption with deliberately "wrong-direction" comparisons — `activated_gen > claim_gen` (line 273), `claimed_by IS NULL` (line 23), `COUNT(*) … <> 1` (lines 95-99) — and none of them gates a transition; `fault-matrix.ts:112-135` writes `claim_gen`/`activated_gen`/`relaunch_count` by hand to construct legal edge rows. Flagging either is flagging the detector.
- **TLA variables the model documents as one-shot.** `firstStarted` (`Scheduler.tla:383`, justified at 167-169: "a task starts for the first time exactly once") and `eventState`'s first-write-wins (`Scheduler.tla:402,463`).
- **The known PR3.8 deferral.** `awaitEvent`'s `ON CONFLICT (run_id, step_name) DO NOTHING` (`store.ts:1561`), the five-field wake predicate and its `runs.wake_step IS NULL` legacy arm (`store.ts:1416-1451`) are the wait-identity gap `BUILD.md:181-192` already owns, with `wait_id` + `runs.active_wait_id` as the named fix. Do not re-report it. A diff that adds an `active` BOOLEAN instead of that identity is in scope and is a finding.

When you report one of these, do not stop at "use a generation". Name (1) the second legitimate occurrence the latch refuses — concretely: a sleep wake, a lost-launch reopen, a chain hop, a replayed await at the same step, a duplicate delivery arriving after a re-claim, or an older process on a rolling deploy; (2) the state the engine ends in and what the caller sees, followed to the terminal reason string if a cap is involved, because this class always surfaces as a healthy subsystem being blamed; (3) the ordinal or token that ALREADY exists to compare against, so the fix is a monotone CAS and not a new column. Then name the mechanism: which conformance case, invariant arm, fault-matrix cell or TLA guard-twin should have caught this and could not — and if the honest answer is that none exists, say so in those words. CLAUDE.md's ladder requires a confirmed finding to produce a mechanism (rung 1 unwritable, rung 2 machine-caught at build, rung 3 machine-caught at test); a hosted reviewer is a detection net of last resort, never a rung. A finding that lands only as a code change is an incomplete finding for this class.
